/// <summary>
/// The text of a member, in every language this assembly supports: <c>[Localized(en: "...", nl: "...", enGb: "...")]</c> on a property, a
/// field, a member of an enum, or a type. <see cref="CodeChops.Idioma.LocalizableText.GetTextByMember(System.Reflection.MemberInfo)"/> gives
/// the text, and <c>GetText()</c> on a value of an enum gives that of its member.
/// </summary>
/// <remarks>
/// The source generator reads the wording as this assembly builds, and writes the text as code. So nothing reads this attribute at
/// run time, and it isn't part of the compiled assembly.
/// </remarks>
[Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.EmbeddedAttribute]
[System.Diagnostics.Conditional("IDIOMA_LOCALIZED_IN_METADATA")]
[System.AttributeUsage(System.AttributeTargets.Property | System.AttributeTargets.Field | System.AttributeTargets.Class | System.AttributeTargets.Struct | System.AttributeTargets.Interface | System.AttributeTargets.Enum, AllowMultiple = false)]
internal sealed class LocalizedAttribute : System.Attribute
{
    /// <summary>
    /// The wording of the member's text in every language: <c>[Localized(en: "...", nl: "...", enGb: "...")]</c>.
    /// </summary>
    /// <remarks>
    /// Name each argument after its language. An unnamed one is a build error (<c>LOC501</c>), because two swapped languages
    /// would go unnoticed. The wording is a constant, so it can't show a value. Write a text with a value as a method of a set.
    /// </remarks>
    /// <param name="en">The wording in <c>en</c>.</param>
    /// <param name="nl">The wording in <c>nl</c>.</param>
    /// <param name="enGb">The wording in <c>en-GB</c>.</param>
    public LocalizedAttribute(string en, string nl, string enGb)
    {
    }
}
